newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe hopes for NATO-Russia deal by end May.
newsitem.headline: Juppe hopes for NATO-Russia deal by end May.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Tuesday he hoped NATO and Russia could reach agreement on a closer relationship by the end of May to ensure the alliance's enlargement did not cause new fractures in Europe.

Speaking after talks with visiting Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov, he told reporters: "We discussed the subject of NATO enlargement and I recalled the French position: we are in favour of the enlargement of NATO provided...it does not reconstitute new fracture lines within Europe.
"I hope we will be able to move forward by the end of May," he said.

Juppe also said France would support Moscow's accession to multilateral institutions such as the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development, the World Trade Organisation and the Paris club of creditor nations "in step with the progress of economic reforms in Russia".
NATO sources said France was keen to host a mini-summit to sign a document enshrining a new cooperative relationship between the 16-nation western defence alliance and Russia.
They said U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin tentatively agreed to aim for a signing on May 27 "somewhere in Europe".
They said the venue might well depend on whether France and the United States settled a dispute over NATO's southern command in time for that date.
Primakov made no comment after the meeting but was due to hold a joint news conference later with French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette.
He is to meet President Jacques Chirac on Wednesday.
Moscow continues to oppose NATO's plans to invite some former communist Warsaw Pact countries in central Europe to join the alliance at a summit to be held in Madrid in July.
Diplomats said Primakov's two-day visit to France was part of a drive to ensure that the inevitable expansion of NATO took place on the least humiliating terms possible for Moscow.
